The U.S. Electorate’s Changing Racial and Ethnic Makeup
item.description: Pew Research Center · The share of eligible voters who are White has declined since 2006, while the Hispanic and Asian shares have nearly doubled. The share of Black eligible voters has changed little over the same period.

item.title: Key facts about Native Hawaiians and Pacific Islanders in the U.S.
item.description: Pew Research Center · About 1.7 million people in the U.S. are Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander (NHPI), tracing their roots to Hawaii, Guam, Samoa or other Pacific Islands in Oceania.

item.title: Key facts about Asians in the U.S.
item.description: Pew Research Center · The number of Asian Americans grew from 11.9 million in 2000 to 24.8 million in 2023.

item.title: 119th Congress brings firsts for women of color
item.description: Pew Research Center · In the Senate, two Black women are serving concurrently for the first time. And in the House, two states and one U.S. territory elected their first Black, Hispanic or Pacific Islander woman lawmaker.

item.title: 119th Congress brings new growth in racial, ethnic diversity to Capitol Hill
item.description: Pew Research Center · Overall, 139 of today’s senators and representatives identify as Black, Hispanic, Asian American or Native American.
